"'''Could've Been'''" is a song by American [[teen-pop]] artist [[Tiffany Darwish|Tiffany]], released as the third single from her debut album, ''[[Tiffany (album)|Tiffany]]'' (1987). The track was written by Lois Blaisch and produced by [[George Tobin]]. Could've Been was discovered by music industry Insiders Don Charles McGovern who worked under the George Tobin Music Production umbrella, McGovern and Schmidt found Lois Blaich singing Could've Been in a Hungry Tiger restaurant in Thousand Oaks, California and knew it was a hit and brought the song to Producer, George Tobbin who then was developing Tiffany. It was released first to North America on November 20, 1987. The song became a hit, topping the charts of the United States, Canada, and Ireland.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: Lois Blaisch said in an interview with [[Songfacts]] that the inspiration for the song came from her oral surgeon ex-boyfriend. She described her ex-boyfriend as someone who led her with lies and that she fell in love with the idea of him, not actually him.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Wiser |first=Carl |date=December 12, 2016 |title=Lois Blaisch ("Could've Been") : Songwriter Interviews |url=https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/lois-blaisch-couldve-been |access-date=October 23, 2024 |website=[[Songfacts]]}}</ref>
sections.text: Lois Blaisch said in an interview with Songfacts that the inspiration for the song came from her oral surgeon ex-boyfriend. She described her ex-boyfriend as someone who led her with lies and that she fell in love with the idea of him, not actually him.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: After debuting at number 86 on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] on November 28, 1987,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/1987-11-28|title=The Hot 100 The week of November 28, 1987|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=November 28, 1987|access-date=November 16, 2018}}</ref> "Could've Been" quickly rose up the chart and spent two weeks at number one in February, becoming [[Tiffany Darwish|Tiffany]]'s second consecutive number-one hit following "[[I Think We're Alone Now]]". She became the first female artist in the rock era to have their first two singles top the chart and the first female teen singer since [[Brenda Lee]] to achieve the feat.<ref name=":1">{{Cite magazine |last=Grein |first=Paul |date=February 6, 1988 |title=Tiffany Gets Off To An Auspicious Start: 'Could've Been' Is Her Second No. 1 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]  |page=6 |volume=100 |issue=6 |issn=0006-2510}}</ref> It was also the third number one single in 15 months following [[Boston (band)|Boston]]'s "[[Amanda (Boston song)|Amanda]]" and [[Michael Jackson]] and [[Siedah Garrett]]'s "[[I Just Can't Stop Loving You]]" to not have a video to be promoted alongside it.<ref name=":1" /> She also became the first artist since 1985 to hold the top spot of the US and UK charts simultaneously with different songs; "Could've Been" was number one in the United States while "I Think We're Alone Now" was number one in the United Kingdom.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Grein |first=Paul |date=February 13, 1988 |title='Phantom' Reappears On Album Chart; Eurythmics, Foreigner Fight Fast Fades |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |page=6 |volume=100 |issue=7 |issn=0006-2510}}</ref>
sections.text: After debuting at number 86 on the US Billboard Hot 100 on November 28, 1987, "Could've Been" quickly rose up the chart and spent two weeks at number one in February, becoming Tiffany's second consecutive number-one hit following "I Think We're Alone Now". She became the first female artist in the rock era to have their first two singles top the chart and the first female teen singer since Brenda Lee to achieve the feat. It was also the third number one single in 15 months following Boston's "Amanda" and Michael Jackson and Siedah Garrett's "I Just Can't Stop Loving You" to not have a video to be promoted alongside it. She also became the first artist since 1985 to hold the top spot of the US and UK charts simultaneously with different songs; "Could've Been" was number one in the United States while "I Think We're Alone Now" was number one in the United Kingdom.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: John Aizlewood from ''[[Number One (magazine)|Number One]]'' declared the song as "mighty", noting how "she croons and how she moves the emotions like a large cheque."<ref name="numberonemagazine">{{cite magazine|first=John|last=Aizlewood|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/57779449@N02/50236262276/in/album-72157715521570932/|title=Singles|magazine=[[Number One (magazine)|Number One]]|date=March 12, 1988|page=44|access-date=March 12, 2023}}</ref>
sections.text: John Aizlewood from Number One declared the song as "mighty", noting how "she croons and how she moves the emotions like a large cheque."

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: "Could've Been" never had an official [[music video]] as network executives felt the lyrics would not sound believable coming from a then 14-year-old Tiffany.<ref name=":0" /> However, a live music video was sent to networks which featured fans singing along to Tiffany's performance.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}}
sections.text: "Could've Been" never had an official music video as network executives felt the lyrics would not sound believable coming from a then 14-year-old Tiffany. However, a live music video was sent to networks which featured fans singing along to Tiffany's performance.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}}
